# Reading path {#sec-reading}

Read in the order of the book: each topic has something to apply now and something for later. The classic papers in the second half give the history behind today's methods.

## By topic

| # | Topic | To apply now | To go deeper |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | GWAS overview | Bush & Moore (2012), [Chapter 11: Genome-wide association studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23300413/), *PLoS Comput Biol* | Uffelmann et al. (2021), "Genome-wide association studies", *Nat Rev Methods Primers* |
| 2 | Genotype QC | Marees et al. (2018), [A tutorial on conducting GWAS](https://doi.org/10.1002/mpr.1608), *Int J Methods Psychiatr Res* | Anderson et al. (2010), [Data quality control in genetic case-control association studies](https://doi.org/10.1038/nprot.2010.116), *Nat Protoc* |
| 3 | QC in biobanks | Turner et al. (2011), [Quality control procedures for GWAS](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21234875/), *Curr Protoc Hum Genet* | — |
| 4 | Population structure | Novembre & Stephens (2008), [Interpreting PCA of spatial population genetic variation](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18425127/), *Nat Genet* | — |
| 5 | PLINK | [PLINK 2.0 documentation](https://www.cog-genomics.org/plink/2.0/) | Chang et al. (2015), "Second-generation PLINK", *GigaScience* |
| 6 | Mixed models | [SAIGE documentation](https://saigegit.github.io/SAIGE-doc/) | Zhou et al. (2018), "Efficiently controlling for case-control imbalance and sample relatedness", *Nat Genet* |
| 7 | Meta-analysis | [METAL documentation](https://genome.sph.umich.edu/wiki/METAL_Documentation) | Willer, Li & Abecasis (2010), "METAL: fast and efficient meta-analysis", *Bioinformatics* |
| 8 | PheWAS | Bush, Oetjens & Crawford (2016), [Unravelling the human genome–phenome relationship](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26875678/), *Nat Rev Genet* | — |
| 9 | Pharmacogenomics | [CPIC guidelines](https://cpicpgx.org/guidelines/) and [PharmVar](https://www.pharmvar.org/) | [PharmCAT](https://pharmcat.org/) documentation |
| 10 | Multi-omics | Ritchie et al. (2015), [Methods of integrating data to uncover genotype–phenotype interactions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25582081/), *Nat Rev Genet* | — |
| 11 | Knowledge graphs | Barrasa & Webber (2023), *Building Knowledge Graphs*, O'Reilly | Bechberger & Perryman (2020), *Graph Databases in Action*, Manning |

## Classic papers

These explain why the field looks the way it does.

**Genetic association**

- Risch & Merikangas (1996). [The future of genetic studies of complex human diseases](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8801636/). *Science*. The argument for association over linkage.
- Cordell & Clayton (2005). [Genetic association studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16182901/). *Lancet*.
- Hirschhorn & Daly (2005). [Genome-wide association studies for common diseases and complex traits](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15716906/). *Nat Rev Genet*.
- Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium (2007). [GWAS of 14,000 cases of seven common diseases and 3,000 shared controls](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17554300/). *Nature*. The study that set the template.
- Maher (2008). [Personal genomes: the case of the missing heritability](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18987709/). *Nature*.
- Hindorff et al. (2009). [Potential etiologic and functional implications of GWAS loci](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19474294/). *PNAS*. The origin of the GWAS Catalog.

**Epistasis and biological knowledge**

- Cordell (2002). [Epistasis: what it means, what it doesn't mean, and statistical methods to detect it in humans](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12351582/). *Hum Mol Genet*.
- Ritchie et al. (2001). [Multifactor-dimensionality reduction reveals high-order interactions](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11404819/). *Am J Hum Genet*.
- Moore (2003). [The ubiquitous nature of epistasis in determining susceptibility to common human diseases](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14614241/). *Hum Hered*.
- Ritchie (2011). [Using biological knowledge to uncover the mystery in the search for epistasis in GWAS](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21158748/). *Ann Hum Genet*.
- Thomas et al. (2009). [Use of pathway information in molecular epidemiology](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21072972/). *Hum Genomics*.

**Phenotypes, biobanks, and study design**

- Thornton-Wells, Moore & Haines (2004). [Genetics, statistics and human disease: analytical retooling for complexity](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15522460/). *Trends Genet*.
- McCarty et al. (2011). [The eMERGE Network](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21269473/). *BMC Med Genomics*. Biobanks linked to electronic health records.
- Peduzzi et al. (1996). [A simulation study of the number of events per variable in logistic regression](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/8970487/). *J Clin Epidemiol*. Why too few cases break a logistic model.

| R | [R for Data Science](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) |

## How to read without stalling your project

One paper per week, tied to the step you're on. After reading, write one line in your analysis plan about what you'll do differently. A read that changes nothing fades within weeks.
